title: ADR-0031: Deploy on One Ubuntu Host with Docker Compose and a Release Tool
heading: Decision
text:
Decision
**Platform.** One Ubuntu host runs Docker Engine and the Compose plugin (2.24 or newer). [`infra/production/compose.yaml`](../../infra/production/compose.yaml) defines three services: `api` (the runtime image, publishing container port 3000 only on the host address and port the installation configures), `postgres` (PostgreSQL 16, pinned by digest, on an internal network with no published port and no outbound route, data in an external named volume that no Compose command removes) and `migrate` (a one-shot service in an `ops` profile that `up` never starts). Containers run read-only with all capabilities dropped and `no-new-privileges`; logs rotate (local driver, 5 × 20 MB).
**Images.** [`infra/production/Dockerfile`](../../infra/production/Dockerfile) builds two targets from one build stage of a release commit: `runtime` (Node.js 24.13.0 on Debian bookworm slim, pinned by digest; production dependencies only; the web build without the `/docs` portal; Oracle Instant Client Basic 19.32 for Linux, downloaded from Oracle's public endpoint and checked against the size and SHA-256 Oracle publishes; user `node`; a loopback healthcheck that follows the internal TLS setting) and `migrate` (the Prisma CLI and `database-deploy`). Images are built on the host from the release tag, labeled with the tag and commit, and never pushed; the Oracle binaries are never committed. The Oracle Free Use Terms shipped with the client cover running it for internal business operations.
**Database roles.** The PostgreSQL superuser only connects through the container's local socket (`peer`), for setup and backups. `ia_mns_migrator` owns the database and applies migrations; `orion_runtime` holds exactly the declared table privileges. A hardened `pg_hba.conf` admits only these two roles over the private network. Roles and passwords are created once, and re-synchronized from the configuration files on demand, by `ia-mns-deploy setup`.
**Secrets.** Configuration lives in `/etc/ia-mns` (root, mode 700): `compose.env` (deployment settings, no secrets), `postgres.env` (superuser, initialization only), `migration.env` (migration credential, `migrate` only), `runtime.env` (the application's environment) and `backup.env`. Each file is root-only (600) and each service receives only its own; the tool refuses a runtime file that holds the migration or administrator credential, development settings or image-owned settings. `ia-mns-deploy init-secrets` generates database passwords and identity keys in place without displaying them. This is a single-host store: files on the host disk, protected by host access control, with the identity encryption key also kept in the company password vault; a secret manager would need a new decision.
**Release tool.** [`ia-mns-deploy`](../../infra/production/bin/ia-mns-deploy) is installed to `/usr/local/sbin` and holds a host-wide lock for every state-changing command. `deploy ia-mns-vX.Y.Z` accepts only an annotated tag on `main` whose required CI check passed (read from GitHub's public API), checks it out as an immutable worktree, continues with that release's own copy of the tool, builds both images, validates the configuration with the new image (`config-check`, no network), takes a mandatory pre-deployment backup, compares the database's migration history with the release (`database-deploy status`) and refuses unknown, failed or modified migrations, runs `migrate`, replaces the API container, waits for health, runs a smoke test through the published address, then records the result. It never runs migrations from the API's command.
**Rollback.** After a failed start, the tool returns to the previous release automatically only when no migration ran during that deployment, because the previous release then meets exactly the schema it ran against. Otherwise it stops and leaves the decision to an operator: `rollback` refuses a release that does not know an applied migration unless `--accept-schema-ahead` records a reviewed decision that the newer migrations are additive; `restore` replaces the database with a backup and keeps the replaced database. Migrations are never edited or reversed in place.
**Backups.** `pg_dump` custom-format archives with a SHA-256, written under `/var/backups/ia-mns` (root, 700): daily by a systemd timer, before every deployment and before every restore, kept 14 and 10 deep by default pending [PH-09](../project/human-actions.md#ph-09). Copies leave the host only encrypted with `age` for a recipient whose private key is kept offline, to a mounted directory or an rsync-over-SSH target. A weekly timer restores the latest backup into a disposable database on an isolated network and checks it against the running release. `status` exits non-zero when the API is unhealthy, the last daily backup is older than 26 hours or the last restore check is older than 8 days; an optional alert command receives failures.
**Verification.** [`infra/production/rehearsal/run.sh`](../../infra/production/rehearsal/run.sh) exercises the real tool and Compose file end to end with synthetic configuration on disposable resources, and runs in CI with the image checks.

title: ADR-0031: Deploy on One Ubuntu Host with Docker Compose and a Release Tool
heading: Rationale
text:
Rationale
One host with Compose is what the owner approved and what the company already operates for PDT Connect; it needs no orchestrator, registry or cloud account. Building on the host from a verified tag removes a registry and its credentials, at the cost of build time on the host. A release-tool script keeps the documented procedure and the executed procedure identical: every step the runbooks name is a command that the rehearsal and CI run. Running each release's own tooling avoids a host tool drifting from the Compose file and Dockerfile it deploys.
Separate roles with a peer-only superuser keep the application unable to change the schema or its own privileges even if it is compromised, and keep the migration credential out of the running process. Automatic rollback is limited to the case where compatibility is proven; a schema the old release does not know is a human decision because an old release may misbehave against it without failing its health check. Backups are not considered real until a restore succeeds, so the restore check performs an actual `pg_restore` and a compatibility check rather than listing the archive.

title: ADR-0031: Deploy on One Ubuntu Host with Docker Compose and a Release Tool
heading: Positive
text:
Positive
One command deploys a verified release with backup, migration, health and smoke checks, and refuses unsafe states before touching the running service.
The application cannot alter its schema or read the migration and administrator credentials.
Backups are restore-tested regularly, and copies leave the host encrypted.
The rehearsal proves install, upgrade, failure handling, rollback and restore on every change in CI.

title: ADR-0031: Deploy on One Ubuntu Host with Docker Compose and a Release Tool
heading: Negative
text:
Negative
Each deployment replaces a single API container: requests are refused for the seconds between stop and readiness.
Images (about 1.3 GB with the Oracle client) are built on the host, which needs network access to GitHub, npm, Docker Hub, Debian and Oracle during builds.
Secrets are files on the host disk; host compromise exposes them.
Retention, external destination, alert channel, proxy hop protection and Oracle transport protection remain owner decisions; until made, `status` and `check-config` report the gaps rather than hiding them.

heading: Operational or Migration Impact
text:
Operational or Migration Impact
Operators follow the [production runbooks](../runbooks/README.md); the infrastructure administrator configures DNS, TLS, the reverse proxy and the host firewall, including Docker's `DOCKER-USER` chain, because published container ports bypass `ufw`.

title: ADR-0032: Resolve Product Selections through a Verified Semantic Catalog
heading: ADR-0032: Resolve Product Selections through a Verified Semantic Catalog
text:
ADR-0032: Resolve Product Selections through a Verified Semantic Catalog
**Status:** accepted
**Date:** 2026-10-11
**Extends:** [ADR-0018](0018-bound-natural-language-sales-to-a-read-only-query-capability.md) (no arbitrary SQL, read-only ERP access), [ADR-0024](0024-interpret-analytics-through-structured-state-and-evaluate-ai-behavior.md) (structured interpretation through the model port) and [ADR-0027](0027-select-the-sales-source-in-the-interface-and-read-each-source-separately.md) (the interface selects the source).

title: ADR-0032: Resolve Product Selections through a Verified Semantic Catalog
heading: Context
text:
Context
On 2026-10-11 the owner asked for a reusable component that identifies products of the VR Master (Pilar da Terra) registration from Portuguese requests such as "Quais produtos são banana fruta?", "Quais produtos são do centro de custo SECOS?" and which products belong to a buyer named in the question, without enumerating every filter or relationship by hand, and without letting a model run SQL against the ERP. The sales capability matches a literal description phrase only; it cannot tell fresh bananas from banana yogurt, and has no notion of cost centers or buyers.
A read-only investigation of the real database on 2026-10-11 found that the answers depend on relationships that are not obvious from column names: cost centers are attached only to the level-1 node of the five-level mercadológico, not to products; the product's buyer is a column of the product registration, while `venda.id_comprador` is a snapshot taken at sale time; the column named "fornecedor fabricante" holds distributors and a placeholder rather than manufacturers; per-store status, barcodes and packaging live in tables the runtime account cannot read. The owner also wants a future Sankhya adapter without redesigning the resolver.

title: ADR-0032: Resolve Product Selections through a Verified Semantic Catalog
heading: Decision
text:
Decision
IA-MNS identifies products through a **semantic catalog** and a resolver with an ERP adapter:
Each ERP adapter supplies a typed, machine-readable catalog (`apps/api/src/features/products/vrmaster/catalog.ts`) of entities, columns with their discovered types, relationships with join columns, direction, cardinality, optionality, evidence (declared constraint, data validation, existing usage), status (`verified`, `validated`, `hypothesis`, `rejected`) and confidence, hierarchies, business dimensions with Portuguese meanings and synonyms, and value conventions. A dimension is usable only when it is `enabled`, every relationship on its path is verified or validated, and the runtime account can read every table on it. The catalog's integrity is checked when it loads, and its required columns, types, nullability and privileges are checked against the live database before the first statement of a process and every ten minutes; any mismatch fails closed.
The model reads the request with one strict tool whose dimension ids come from the catalog, and, for classifications, chooses among numbered **real candidate nodes** the application retrieved (with their paths, counts and up to three example descriptions) with a second strict tool. Named records (buyers, cost centers) are matched by the application from the person's own words, never by the model. Every value is grounded in the person's text, resolved to ERP records, merged, checked for contradictions and executed by the application.
The adapter compiles the validated selection to parameterized SQL using only catalog identifiers: the outer query reads only the product table, every relationship is a semi-join, so one-to-many paths cannot duplicate products, and exclusions are null-safe. Each request runs in a read-only, rolled-back transaction with the existing VR Master limits; lists are bounded to 200 products with an exact total.
Product lookup is a separate corporate-agent capability (`products`, permission `products:read`, granted automatically to no provider until the owner decides) that identifies products and never calculates sales. Its answer states, for every criterion, the records or classification paths it resolved to and the business rule of the relationship. It runs only when the interface selects Pilar da Terra (VR Master) or Tudo.
Classification paths, product counts and up to three example product descriptions per candidate may be sent to OpenAI to choose among candidates. Buyer names and other personal data, prices, costs, stock and sales never are: options that hold personal data appear only in the structured result, and the model sees a placeholder.

title: ADR-0032: Resolve Product Selections through a Verified Semantic Catalog
heading: Rationale
text:
Rationale
Selecting among enumerated, real candidates keeps the model's strength (understanding that "banana fruta" excludes chips, yogurts and raw materials) while the application keeps every guarantee: no free text reaches SQL, every value is an ERP record or a bound literal, and every interpretation is visible to the person. The live regression on 2026-10-11 confirmed that the model, given the candidates, chose the fresh-banana nodes, kept sweet corn out of "doces", and excluded a product of another brand misfiled under a brand node; the same model asked for clarification when "banana" had different kinds.
Encoding the relationships with their evidence, rather than letting a model infer joins from schema names, is what prevents wrong answers that look plausible: a product-level cost center or a manufacturer column would have produced complete but false lists. Keeping the catalog as code gives it type checking, review and a single deployable source; verifying it against the live schema protects against ERP upgrades.
Classification labels are product catalog data, not personal, customer or financial data; sending a bounded sample is the smallest input that lets the model judge candidates such as a node named after a producer. Buyer resolution needs no model judgment, so names stay inside IA-MNS.

heading: Alternatives Considered
text: Alternatives Considered

title: ADR-0032: Resolve Product Selections through a Verified Semantic Catalog
heading: Model-generated SQL over the schema
text:
Model-generated SQL over the schema
Rejected: it contradicts ADR-0018, cannot be validated reliably, and would still need the relationship knowledge above to be correct.

title: ADR-0032: Resolve Product Selections through a Verified Semantic Catalog
heading: Literal description matching only (the sales approach)
text:
Literal description matching only (the sales approach)
Rejected as the general mechanism: "banana" matches yogurts, candies, sunscreen and raw materials, and description text cannot express cost centers or buyers. It remains a dimension (`description`) and the fallback the person can choose.

title: ADR-0032: Resolve Product Selections through a Verified Semantic Catalog
heading: Embeddings or a vector database
text:
Embeddings or a vector database
Not adopted: the classification already encodes the product taxonomy, candidate retrieval over it is fast (about one second on the real data) and exact, and no measured case required semantic search beyond what the model does among candidates. It would add infrastructure and a second copy of ERP data.

title: ADR-0032: Resolve Product Selections through a Verified Semantic Catalog
heading: A catalog generated automatically from foreign keys
text:
A catalog generated automatically from foreign keys
Rejected as the runtime source: the investigation found a declared-but-unused brand column, a fiscal column that looks like a classification and an undeclared relationship that is only a snapshot. Discovery is automated (`products:catalog` lists unreviewed foreign keys and checks invariants), but exposure requires review.

title: ADR-0032: Resolve Product Selections through a Verified Semantic Catalog
heading: Consequences
text: Consequences

title: ADR-0032: Resolve Product Selections through a Verified Semantic Catalog
heading: Positive
text:
Positive
New product questions combine verified dimensions without new SQL; adding a dimension is a reviewed catalog change plus tests.
The resolver core (catalog model, interpretation, state, grounding, merge, answers) is ERP-neutral; a Sankhya adapter adds a catalog and an Oracle compiler and source behind the same port.
Answers explain the relationship used, so a business reader can check or correct the interpretation.

title: ADR-0032: Resolve Product Selections through a Verified Semantic Catalog
heading: Negative
text:
Negative
Two model calls per classification criterion: turns take about 3 to 20 seconds on the real data; transient provider errors fail the turn, as other model calls do, without automatic retries.
The catalog must be maintained when the ERP changes; a changed column disables the capability until reviewed.
Product descriptions and classification labels now reach the model provider under `store:false`, which does not establish zero provider retention.
Results include inactive products until the per-store status becomes readable, and model judgment can differ between runs for borderline products; both are stated in the answer and in the documentation.

title: ADR-0032: Resolve Product Selections through a Verified Semantic Catalog
heading: Operational or Migration Impact
text:
Operational or Migration Impact
The agent reply contract gains two additive result kinds and two progress stages; earlier stored replies are unchanged.
A new permission `products:read` exists; owners receive it, other people need an explicit grant until the owner decides on provider grants.
Enabling store status, packaging or family requires column-level SELECT grants on the VR Master tables named in the human actions, then validation and a catalog change.

title: ADR-0033: Use One Reader and the Existing Administrator per ERP
heading: ADR-0033: Use One Reader and the Existing Administrator per ERP
text:
ADR-0033: Use One Reader and the Existing Administrator per ERP
**Status:** accepted
**Date:** 2026-10-11

title: ADR-0033: Use One Reader and the Existing Administrator per ERP
heading: Context
text:
Context
IA-MNS reads Sankhya Oracle and VRMaster PostgreSQL. Earlier investigation used broader credentials alongside runtime configuration, and PH-29 requested removal and rotation of the temporary VRMaster Discovery credentials. The owner has now explicitly decided the account topology and authorized ongoing read-only Discovery with the existing administrative users.

title: ADR-0033: Use One Reader and the Existing Administrator per ERP
heading: Decision
text:
Decision
Each ERP has exactly two IA-MNS access identities: a dedicated least-privilege runtime reader and the existing administrator, also used by Codex for Discovery. Sankhya runtime is `IA_MNS_RO` (provisioning pending); VRMaster runtime is the already provisioned `ia_mns`. Do not create a third account dedicated to Discovery, replace the existing administrator or rotate its credentials merely because Discovery ended.
Preserve `VRMASTER_DB_USER_FULLACESS` and `VRMASTER_DB_PASSWORD_FULLACESS`; add `SANKHYA_DB_USER_FULLACESS` and `SANKHYA_DB_PASSWORD_FULLACESS`. Administrative credentials belong in ignored `.env.discovery.local`, explicitly read by development tools. Runtime configuration, processes, client builds and deployment must not receive them or fall back to them.
Discovery permits only reading and inspecting task-relevant schemas, objects, relationships and data, subject to project confidentiality. Read-only transactions are additional protection, not sufficient containment for an administrator. ERP mutations, including DML, DDL, grants, revocations and procedures with side effects, require explicit owner authorization. For implementations needing more runtime access, identify minimum privileges, prepare reviewed scripts and execute within that authorization; the current architecture task explicitly prohibits all real ERP account/privilege changes.
This refines ERP access only. Application-owned PostgreSQL runtime/migration identities remain separate. [ERP access policy](../security/erp-database-access.md) owns current controls and procedures.

title: ADR-0033: Use One Reader and the Existing Administrator per ERP
heading: Rationale
text:
Rationale
The owner's definitive decision retains the existing operational administrator and permits necessary development investigation without a redundant third account. Separating credential delivery preserves the runtime reader boundary. Fixed inspection queries, explicit projections, bounded reads, local evidence and human authorization for mutations compensate for some exposure, but do not convert an administrator into a restricted database reader.

Share administrative credentials with runtime

text: Consequences

title: ADR-0033: Use One Reader and the Existing Administrator per ERP

Positive

Credential names remain compatible and the existing ERP administrators are preserved.

title: ADR-0033: Use One Reader and the Existing Administrator per ERP
heading: Negative
text:
Negative
A Discovery process still holds administrative capability; reviewed operations and confidentiality controls remain necessary.
Local isolation and runtime configuration tests do not certify actual database grants or sandbox arbitrary SQL.

heading: Operational or Migration Impact
text:
Operational or Migration Impact
Separate local administrative credential delivery and provision `IA_MNS_RO` before combined Sankhya runtime acceptance (PH-08).
PH-29 becomes credential isolation and maintenance, not removal of the administrative identity.
This decision does not itself execute ERP provisioning or grant scripts.

title: ADR-0034: Apply Verified Product Selections to Sales without Materializing Display Lists
heading: ADR-0034: Apply Verified Product Selections to Sales without Materializing Display Lists
text:
ADR-0034: Apply Verified Product Selections to Sales without Materializing Display Lists
**Status:** proposed
**Date:** 2026-10-12
**Extends:** [ADR-0032](0032-resolve-product-selections-through-a-verified-semantic-catalog.md), [ADR-0018](0018-bound-natural-language-sales-to-a-read-only-query-capability.md), [ADR-0027](0027-select-the-sales-source-in-the-interface-and-read-each-source-separately.md).

title: ADR-0034: Apply Verified Product Selections to Sales without Materializing Display Lists
heading: Context
text:
Context
The owner requested integration of the existing resolver with sales. Product answers list at most 200 registrations, while a valid classification or indirect filter can identify thousands. Passing that display list to sales would silently undercount. The registration catalogs already own reviewed relationships, semantics, validation and compilers; sales owns its reference grain, monetary/quantity/weight definitions and date bounds.

title: ADR-0034: Apply Verified Product Selections to Sales without Materializing Display Lists
heading: Decision
text:
Decision
The implementation under review composes a product-owned coordinator through a sales-owned resolution port. The resolver interprets only the product conditions of an otherwise validated sales request and retains its existing grounding and ambiguity rules. Its adapter revalidates access/metadata and compiles complete key membership. The sales adapter adds this internal, bound key subquery as a semi-join to its reference SQL. Neither model nor HTTP caller supplies SQL, identifiers or product codes.
Membership uses the current registration at execution, equally for both comparison periods. A current product buyer filter does not become a historical sale-time buyer filter. Existing monetary measures, reference joins, unit handling and transaction limits remain authoritative. A scoped request chooses one ERP; ordinary literal sales retain the existing independent `Tudo` behavior. Explicit references can reuse a same-source, catalog-versioned lookup; unrelated new sales do not inherit it. Semantic sales requires both existing permissions on every turn.

title: ADR-0034: Apply Verified Product Selections to Sales without Materializing Display Lists
heading: Rationale
text:
Rationale
This completes the separation in ADR-0032 without making sales depend on product internals or adding a second resolver. Predicate compilation preserves complete membership without large id arrays, Oracle list limits or display truncation. Persisted context holds selections, not SQL. Using current registration is consistent with the verified product concepts; historical classification/responsibility needs separate evidence and is outside this request.

text: Alternatives Considered

title: ADR-0034: Apply Verified Product Selections to Sales without Materializing Display Lists
heading: Pass the displayed product ids
text:
Pass the displayed product ids
Rejected because the display is intentionally incomplete. Raising its limit would introduce expensive materialization and still require refusal above a new arbitrary cap.

title: ADR-0034: Apply Verified Product Selections to Sales without Materializing Display Lists
heading: Let the sales interpreter generate joins
text:
Let the sales interpreter generate joins
Rejected because it would duplicate semantic ownership and expose execution to unchecked model SQL.

title: ADR-0034: Apply Verified Product Selections to Sales without Materializing Display Lists
heading: Consequences
text: Consequences

title: ADR-0034: Apply Verified Product Selections to Sales without Materializing Display Lists
heading: Positive
text:
Positive
Complete scoped totals, no expansion of one-to-many relations, explicit interpretation/provenance, and reusable per-ERP compiler behavior.
No ERP grants, schema changes or new runtime credentials are required for the already enabled dimensions.

title: ADR-0034: Apply Verified Product Selections to Sales without Materializing Display Lists
heading: Negative
text:
Negative
Semantic requests add resolver work within the existing finite turn deadline; unavailable paths or ambiguity block sales rather than produce partial totals.
Reference semantics can exclude identified registrations with no eligible sales. Current membership cannot answer historical responsibility questions.

title: ADR-0034: Apply Verified Product Selections to Sales without Materializing Display Lists
heading: Operational or Migration Impact
text:
Operational or Migration Impact
Agent sales context has a versioned envelope that upgrades existing sales state; legacy sales HTTP remains literal and unchanged.
Sales results add optional product-selection provenance; generated OpenAPI/SDK and the existing result UI consume it. Product/aggregate display bounds remain separate from total membership.
This record remains proposed for repository review; it does not change accepted ADR history or authorize deployment.

title: ADR-0035: Compose Conversations over Authorized Evidence and Semantic Tools
heading: ADR-0035: Compose Conversations over Authorized Evidence and Semantic Tools
text:
ADR-0035: Compose Conversations over Authorized Evidence and Semantic Tools
**Status:** accepted
**Date:** 2026-10-13
**Supersedes:** [ADR-0018](0018-bound-natural-language-sales-to-a-read-only-query-capability.md), [ADR-0019](0019-compose-a-corporate-agent-with-durable-conversations.md) and [ADR-0024](0024-interpret-analytics-through-structured-state-and-evaluate-ai-behavior.md), only their fixed-response routing and blanket figure-free model-context restrictions. Domain semantics, authorization, read-only execution, deterministic calculations and durable history remain accepted.

title: ADR-0035: Compose Conversations over Authorized Evidence and Semantic Tools
heading: Context
text:
Context
The capability router deliberately prevented free-form answers and withheld numerical results from the model. As a result, a request to summarize an already completed sales query could become an unsupported new query. The owner authorized implementation of the autonomy proposal, delegated incremental technical decisions, and approved necessary business-data transmission to OpenAI on 2026-10-12. Personal-data and deployment prerequisites remain category-specific.
This record accepts that explicitly approved direction after implementation review of the provider, evidence, authorization and semantic-query boundaries; acceptance does not claim completed rollout or corporate legal verification.

title: ADR-0035: Compose Conversations over Authorized Evidence and Semantic Tools
heading: Decision
text:
Decision
Use one bounded Responses tool loop beside the existing strict interpretation adapter. The conversational model may answer directly, retrieve owned evidence and attachments, or propose a registered analytical tool. The server validates arguments, authorization, source, work limits, evidence and final fact references. No SQL, arbitrary network, hosted execution or ERP write tool is exposed.
Compose existing sales measures with validated time/product dimensions through a structured semantic plan. Reuse the existing Product Resolver and complete product membership, reviewed sales query grain and decimal calculations. Several measures in one ERP share a read-only database snapshot; different ERPs remain separate. New business definitions still require catalog/query validation.
Permit minimized real operational evidence under the owner's approval. Preserve `store:false`, foreground processing, no automatic retries, no SDK payload logging and local authoritative history. Derived prose inherits all transmitted evidence permissions, not only cited ones. Numeric ERP claims bind to exact server facts. Metadata traces exclude confidential content; provider reasoning continuation exists only in memory for the current turn.
Keep limited owner-classified operational attachments and explicit presentation preferences within conversation lifecycle. The model cannot persist preferences, promote semantic candidates, change authorizations or rewrite business rules. Attachments are user evidence, not ERP truth; removing one invalidates dependent responses. Binary office documents, PDFs, URLs, macros and archive extraction remain unsupported; text/CSV and bounded PNG/JPEG have explicit limits.
This direction partially replaces the application-authored-response and figure-free conversational-context constraints of ADR-0018, ADR-0019 and ADR-0024. Their domain semantics, permission checks, durability, no-write boundary, deterministic arithmetic and curated-evaluation obligations remain. A `legacy` configuration provides routing rollback while the new code retains derived-reply authorization. Rolling back to an older binary that does not understand new reply fields is not supported.

title: ADR-0035: Compose Conversations over Authorized Evidence and Semantic Tools
heading: Rationale
text:
Rationale
General conversation and typed tools handle families of requests without phrase lists. A provider-neutral port and existing SDK suffice; a second agent framework or business-rule layer would add responsibility without supplying data authorization. Local evidence makes continued conversation and revocation auditable, while exact substitution limits numerical invention. Schema validation cannot prove that qualitative prose correctly interprets every fact; evaluated behavior and explicit uncertainty remain necessary.

Expose generated SQL or unrestricted database exploration

title: ADR-0035: Compose Conversations over Authorized Evidence and Semantic Tools

Summaries, explanations and rewrites reuse authorized results without new ERP reads.
Semantic composition reuses existing reconciled logic and product selection rather than duplicating it.
Permission inheritance and attachment deletion cover derived prose and acceptance replay.

title: ADR-0036: Add WhatsApp as an Agent Channel Authorized by Owner-Linked Numbers
heading: ADR-0036: Add WhatsApp as an Agent Channel Authorized by Owner-Linked Numbers
text:
ADR-0036: Add WhatsApp as an Agent Channel Authorized by Owner-Linked Numbers
**Status:** proposed
**Date:** 2026-10-13

title: ADR-0036: Add WhatsApp as an Agent Channel Authorized by Owner-Linked Numbers
heading: Context
text:
Context
The owner asked for WhatsApp as a fourth way to use IA-MNS, beside the direct web application, Sankhya and PDT Connect ([ADR-0023](0023-serve-one-frontend-to-three-surfaces-with-host-identity-proofs.md)). The product decisions are fixed: a dedicated corporate number operated only through Meta's official WhatsApp Business Platform Cloud API, without coexistence, migration, human attendance or an intermediary provider; access only for people whose number an authenticated owner linked to their IA-MNS account, with no self-service of any kind; the same agent, tools, permissions, history and context; and a reactive, text-first first version.
WhatsApp differs from the existing surfaces in three ways that need an architectural answer. There is no browser and no IA-MNS session: each message arrives as a signed server-to-server webhook from Meta, and the only statement about the sender is the number (and, since 2026, a business-scoped user identifier) that Meta reports. The webhook must be acknowledged quickly while an agent turn can take up to 90 seconds. And a reply is an external effect that cannot be recalled, without an idempotency key, so delivery, retries and revocation must be explicit ([delivery and side effects](../architecture/delivery-and-side-effects.md)).

title: ADR-0036: Add WhatsApp as an Agent Channel Authorized by Owner-Linked Numbers
heading: Decision
text:
Decision
**The number is an identity attribute, not a sign-in method.** The identity module owns `identity_whatsapp_links`: at most one number per Person and one Person per number. Only owners set, change or remove it, with the administrative safeguards of [ADR-0025](0025-administer-the-authentication-policy-within-fixed-safeguards.md), and each change is audited in the same transaction. It never opens an IA-MNS session and grants no permission by itself. Matching is exact on E.164 digits plus one deterministic alias (the legacy eight-digit form of a Brazilian mobile, part of the uniqueness rule); a business-scoped user identifier is recorded only when Meta reports it together with the linked number, and a disagreement is refused.
**Identity decides authorization per message.** A composition port gives the channel identity's decision for a verified sender: exactly one active Person, the link version, and that Person's effective permissions computed from trusted state as for a token. The channel asks again before processing, after the agent answers and before each reply part, so revocation applies to work already in progress. Unknown or refused senders are ignored silently and never stored.
**A separate `whatsapp` module adapts Meta to the existing agent.** It owns the signed webhook, a PostgreSQL inbox and outbox, per-Person ordering, the Graph API client, commands and text formatting. It holds no business capability. The agent module publishes its single `CorporateAgent` at composition, and an agent-owned adapter exposes "continue a channel conversation" and "submit and await a turn" with the same request-id replay, concurrency limit, lease recovery and failure classification as the web. Conversations record their starting channel (`agent_conversations.channel`) as metadata only.
**Delivery is durable and conservative.** Authorized messages are recorded before the webhook is acknowledged, deduplicated by Meta message id and processed asynchronously under leases. A reply part is retried only when Meta proves it was not accepted; a timeout or lost response is recorded as an unknown outcome and never resent. Replies stay inside the 24-hour customer service window; nothing is sent proactively.
**The channel can be stopped without a deployment.** The `channels.whatsapp` operational parameter ([ADR-0028](0028-administer-operational-parameters-separately-from-secrets-and-bootstrap-configuration.md)) switches processing and sending on or off for the next message; credentials remain secrets in the environment.

title: ADR-0036: Add WhatsApp as an Agent Channel Authorized by Owner-Linked Numbers
heading: Rationale
text:
Rationale
Keeping the number inside identity reuses the one place that already decides who a person is, what they may do and how changes are audited; treating it as an external link (`identity_external_identities`) would have made it a sign-in method that the existing flows could unlink, merge and prove, none of which applies. Recomputing permissions per message avoids a parallel session model for a channel without a browser, and repeating the check before every external effect is what makes revocation effective for messages already being answered.
A separate module keeps Meta's specifics (signatures, payload shape, identifiers, Graph errors, service window) out of the agent and identity, matching the module contract, while the published agent instance guarantees one turn lifecycle for every channel instead of a second agent. PostgreSQL already provides the transactional claims, uniqueness and durability the workflow needs; a broker would add infrastructure to the single-host deployment ([ADR-0031](0031-deploy-on-one-ubuntu-host-with-docker-compose-and-a-release-tool.md)) without a requirement that PostgreSQL cannot meet.
The costs are accepted: a phone number is a weaker credential than the existing sign-in methods, the channel adds three tables and background workers to the API process, and conservative delivery may leave a reply undelivered when its outcome is unknown rather than risk sending it twice.

heading: Alternatives Considered
text: Alternatives Considered

title: ADR-0036: Add WhatsApp as an Agent Channel Authorized by Owner-Linked Numbers

Self-service linking (codes or links sent to WhatsApp)
Rejected by the owner: access must be granted only by an administrator. It would also add an enrollment surface to attack.

title: ADR-0036: Add WhatsApp as an Agent Channel Authorized by Owner-Linked Numbers
heading: Link the number as a third external identity provider
text:
Link the number as a third external identity provider
Rejected: external links are proven sign-in methods with their own flows (first access, linking, consolidation offers). A WhatsApp number is never proven to IA-MNS by the person, never signs in, and is managed only by owners.

title: ADR-0036: Add WhatsApp as an Agent Channel Authorized by Owner-Linked Numbers
heading: A Business Solution Provider or WhatsApp App coexistence
text:
A Business Solution Provider or WhatsApp App coexistence
Rejected by the owner unless a technical need is proven; none was found. The Cloud API offers webhooks, signatures and sending directly.

title: ADR-0036: Add WhatsApp as an Agent Channel Authorized by Owner-Linked Numbers
heading: Synchronous processing inside the webhook
text:
Synchronous processing inside the webhook
Rejected: agent turns can outlast Meta's delivery expectations, and a crash would lose the message. The inbox records it before acknowledgement.

heading: A separate agent or WhatsApp-specific business tools
text:
A separate agent or WhatsApp-specific business tools
Rejected: it would duplicate capabilities, permissions and context and let the channels drift.

title: ADR-0036: Add WhatsApp as an Agent Channel Authorized by Owner-Linked Numbers
heading: Consequences
text: Consequences

title: ADR-0036: Add WhatsApp as an Agent Channel Authorized by Owner-Linked Numbers
heading: Positive
text:
Positive
One agent, one permission model and one history across all four ways in; WhatsApp conversations are visible and continuable on the web.
Revocation (number removal or change, disabled Person, consolidation, switch off) stops replies that were still being prepared.
No new external service, broker or provider dependency besides Meta.

title: ADR-0036: Add WhatsApp as an Agent Channel Authorized by Owner-Linked Numbers
heading: Negative
text:
Negative
Possession of a linked phone (or its WhatsApp session) is enough to act as the Person; there is no second factor. Read-only capabilities only; a write or sensitive capability needs a new decision before it can reach this channel.
Business answers transit Meta and remain on devices outside IA-MNS control.
An uncertain send is not repeated, so a reply can be lost in a Meta incident; the answer remains in the web history.

title: ADR-0036: Add WhatsApp as an Agent Channel Authorized by Owner-Linked Numbers
heading: Operational or Migration Impact
text:
Operational or Migration Impact
Four additive migrations: the identity links, the conversation channel, the parameter key and the channel tables. Older application versions ignore them.
Production activation needs Meta account actions, the verified dedicated number, secrets, an HTTPS webhook on the public origin and owner approval of the processing boundary ([PH-32 to PH-35](../project/human-actions.md#ph-32)); the [runbook](../runbooks/whatsapp-channel.md) covers activation and rollback.

title: ADR-0037: Grant Identified Per-Source Permissions to People and Groups with Data Restrictions
heading: ADR-0037: Grant Identified Per-Source Permissions to People and Groups with Data Restrictions
text:
ADR-0037: Grant Identified Per-Source Permissions to People and Groups with Data Restrictions
**Status:** proposed
**Date:** 2026-10-20

title: ADR-0037: Grant Identified Per-Source Permissions to People and Groups with Data Restrictions
heading: Context

title: ADR-0037: Grant Identified Per-Source Permissions to People and Groups with Data Restrictions
heading: Decision
text:
Decision
**One grantable permission per source and data area, each with a stable code.** The catalog is composed from descriptors the owning modules declare: `sales_sankhya:read` (SNK-VEN-01), `sales_vrmaster:read` (VRM-VEN-01), `products_sankhya:read` (SNK-PRD-01) and `products_vrmaster:read` (VRM-PRD-01); owners keep `identity:admin` (IAM-ADM-01). `sales:read` and `products:read` remain as capability permissions that identity derives whenever a source permission of the family is held; they are never granted. Existing grants and saved automatic grants of the former names become the grants of both sources they covered, so nobody gains or loses access.
**Restrictions are declared and enforced by the module that owns the data.** Each permission lists the dimensions it can be narrowed by, each with a code. Sankhya sales: company (EMP, `CAB.CODEMP`), project/sector (PRJ, `ITE.AD_CODPROJ` with its subprojects), seller (VEN, `CAB.CODVEND`), product group (GRP, `PRO.CODGRUPOPROD` with its subgroups) and result center (CR, `CAB.CODCENCUS` with the centers below it). VR Master sales: store (LOJ, `venda.id_loja`), sale-time buyer (COM, `venda.id_comprador`), section cost center (CC, with the centers below it) and classification (MER, any mercadológico level with the levels below it). The sales readers add the restriction as a bound predicate to the reviewed reference SQL, filtering rows without changing joins or the DISTINCT projection. Product permissions have no restriction: the registrations are shared by every company and store.
**A grant is a conjunction, a person's access a union.** Within a grant, the values of one dimension are alternatives and every restricted dimension must match; a grant without restrictions admits every row. A Person's scope for a permission is the union of its own grant and its groups' grants (any unrestricted grant admits everything). Provider policy grants a permission, unrestricted, only when the Person has no explicit grant of it, so an owner narrows an automatic grant by granting it explicitly. Owners hold everything unrestricted. A grant restricted by a dimension its permission no longer declares cannot be enforced and is ignored.
**Groups belong to identity.** Owners create, rename and delete groups, add and remove active members and grant permissions to groups, with the same owner, second-factor and recent-confirmation checks as all administration; every change is audited in its transaction with permission codes and value counts, never labels.
**Restriction values are real records.** Owners choose values from a read-only directory the sales module supplies; identity reads each submitted value back from the source and stores its label, so neither codes nor labels come from the browser.
**Access is computed now and carried with each turn.** The agent, the legacy sales route and the WhatsApp channel obtain the current permissions and scopes of the principal from identity through a composition port instead of trusting the access-token scopes alone, so narrowing or revocation applies to the next request. Tokens keep the permission strings only.
**Denials are identified and server-written.** When a request needs a source the person may not read, the agent answers with a fixed message listing each missing permission's code, title and source and asking the person to give the codes to support; in conversational mode the model can only request this answer through a dedicated tool, never phrase it. A selected source that is denied appears in the answer as a denied section beside the others. A product selection that names a sale-time buyer outside the person's VR Master scope is refused with the permission and the exact values support must release. Every restricted result records its scope and carries a caveat that it is not the source's total; history and evidence are shown only to readers whose current scope covers the recorded one.

title: ADR-0037: Grant Identified Per-Source Permissions to People and Groups with Data Restrictions
heading: Rationale
text:
Rationale
Splitting permissions by source matches how the business sees the data (MNS in Sankhya, Pilar da Terra in VR Master) and how restrictions differ between them; a single permission with a "source" restriction would have mixed dimensions of two ERPs in one grant. Keeping derived capability permissions avoids rewriting every capability gate and the readability of existing history, while per-source checks happen where each source is read.
Declaring dimensions with the queries that enforce them keeps identity free of ERP knowledge and makes an undeclared dimension impossible to grant. Filtering inside the reviewed SQL, rather than filtering returned rows, means totals are computed only from admitted rows and no unadmitted row leaves the ERP. The union-of-conjunctions model is the exact meaning of "this group sees company 1, and this person also sees seller 12"; flattening it per dimension would grant combinations nobody granted.
Computing access now per request costs one identity read per agent request, but it gives immediate revocation, which a 10-minute token cannot, and avoids putting value lists into tokens. Server-written denials guarantee that the codes support receives are exact; a model could omit or invent them.

title: ADR-0037: Grant Identified Per-Source Permissions to People and Groups with Data Restrictions
heading: Alternatives Considered
text: Alternatives Considered

title: ADR-0037: Grant Identified Per-Source Permissions to People and Groups with Data Restrictions
heading: Restrictions in the access token
text:
Restrictions in the access token
Putting the scopes into a token claim would avoid the identity read, but it would delay revocation by the token lifetime, enlarge every token with value lists, and require the shared verifier to understand an IA-MNS-specific claim.

title: ADR-0037: Grant Identified Per-Source Permissions to People and Groups with Data Restrictions
heading: One permission with a source restriction
text:
One permission with a source restriction
Keeping `sales:read` and treating the source as a restriction dimension would avoid renaming grants, but would put Sankhya and VR Master dimensions in one grant, make codes depend on restrictions, and contradict the owner's request to separate permissions by source.

title: ADR-0037: Grant Identified Per-Source Permissions to People and Groups with Data Restrictions
heading: Product registration restrictions
text:
Product registration restrictions
Restricting product lookup by classification, buyer or cost center was considered and deferred: the registration is shared and not financial, and enforcing it would require changes across candidate search, counts and examples of both resolvers. Sales figures, the sensitive data, are restricted.

title: ADR-0037: Grant Identified Per-Source Permissions to People and Groups with Data Restrictions
heading: Consequences
text: Consequences

title: ADR-0037: Grant Identified Per-Source Permissions to People and Groups with Data Restrictions
heading: Positive
text:
Positive
Owners grant once to a group, narrow any grant to real ERP records, and see where each effective permission comes from; people see their own codes in Minha conta.
Refusals tell the person and support exactly what to release, on the web and on WhatsApp.
Restricted figures are computed in the ERP from admitted rows only and are labeled as partial.

title: ADR-0037: Grant Identified Per-Source Permissions to People and Groups with Data Restrictions
heading: Negative
text:
Negative
Each agent and legacy sales request reads the Person's grants and groups from the database.
Hierarchical restrictions are compared as selected when checking history coverage; an equivalent narrower restatement can hide older answers. Conflicts between a product selection and a restriction are detected only for VR Master buyers; for hierarchical dimensions the restricted SQL still applies and the caveat explains it.
Consolidating two Persons can keep only the surviving Person's restricted grant when two restricted grants cannot be united exactly.
History computed before a restriction existed is unrestricted and is no longer shown to a person whose access becomes restricted.

title: ADR-0037: Grant Identified Per-Source Permissions to People and Groups with Data Restrictions
heading: Operational or Migration Impact
text:
Operational or Migration Impact
Two migrations: an additive one for groups and restrictions and a data step converting `sales:read`/`products:read` grants and the saved automatic grants. The data step is not reversible in place; an older application needs a backup restore. `IA_MNS_PROVIDER_GRANTS=sankhya:sales:read` keeps its meaning.
The Sankhya restriction by result center needs `SELECT` on `TSICUS` for the Runtime reader, prepared in the reviewed grant template and awaiting the owner ([PH-36](../project/human-actions.md#ph-36)); until then that dimension cannot be granted.
Whether a Sankhya link should keep granting VR Master sales automatically is the owner's decision ([PH-13](../project/human-actions.md#ph-13)); the default preserves the previous behavior.

title: ADR-0038: Join Default User Groups after Verified Provider Sign-In
heading: ADR-0038: Join Default User Groups after Verified Provider Sign-In
text:
ADR-0038: Join Default User Groups after Verified Provider Sign-In
**Status:** proposed
**Date:** 2026-10-21
**Supersedes:** [ADR-0022](0022-own-the-ia-mns-identity-with-verified-external-links.md) and [ADR-0028](0028-administer-operational-parameters-separately-from-secrets-and-bootstrap-configuration.md), only their automatic permission grants by external link; [ADR-0037](0037-grant-identified-per-source-permissions-to-people-and-groups-with-data-restrictions.md), only its provider-policy fallback. Identity proof, owner safeguards and ordinary group grants remain unchanged.

title: ADR-0038: Join Default User Groups after Verified Provider Sign-In
heading: Context
text:
Context
The owner requested replacing automatic permission grants with a default user group for each external system. Groups already own per-source permissions and their restrictions; a parallel automatic permission policy obscures the origin and scope of access.

title: ADR-0038: Join Default User Groups after Verified Provider Sign-In
heading: Decision
text:
Decision
Owners select an existing group independently for PDT Connect and Sankhya, or no group, in **Administração → Parâmetros → Grupo de Usuário padrão por vínculo**. Identity owns these selections in `identity_provider_groups`, separately from operational parameters. Changes require recent strong owner authentication, the version read, and transactional audit.
After successful provider sign-in, including first-access provisioning and direct provider callbacks, the active Person joins the selected group before the access token is issued. Repeated sign-ins are idempotent. The group supplies its ordinary grants and restrictions, united with other personal and group grants. A link alone, owner directory association, local-password login, refresh or WhatsApp message never triggers membership. Invalid proofs and disabled people acquire no membership.
Membership is persistent. Clearing or changing a default and unlinking a provider do not remove memberships. Removing someone manually is effective immediately, but the next verified sign-in to the same provider rejoins the current default. Changing a default affects future sign-ins only; it does not move existing members. A selected group cannot be deleted until the owner clears or replaces its selection. Selection changes and sign-in assignments serialize on the provider row.

title: ADR-0038: Join Default User Groups after Verified Provider Sign-In
heading: Rationale
text:
Rationale
The existing group model provides one permission and restriction mechanism. Persistent membership makes access explainable in the group and Person screens and preserves it across sign-in methods. Automatic removal would need additional provenance and revocation semantics that the owner did not request.

title: ADR-0038: Join Default User Groups after Verified Provider Sign-In
heading: Alternatives Considered
text:
Alternatives Considered
Retain a permission checklist per provider: duplicates group authorization and does not meet the requested membership behavior.
Treat membership as a transient projection of every stored link: changes access during unrelated logins and does not represent entry through the indicated system.

title: ADR-0038: Join Default User Groups after Verified Provider Sign-In
heading: Consequences
text:
Consequences
Every automatic membership is audited once and appears as an ordinary group membership.
Groups grant no owner role. Personal restrictions do not override a broader group grant; owners must restrict the default group itself when needed.
Existing automatic permissions cease to apply. Migration `202610210001_identity_provider_groups` seeds both selections empty; owners must select groups and review their permissions. Existing explicit grants, memberships, historical parameter rows and audit are retained. `access.providerGrants` is no longer exposed or accepted by the parameter API; `IA_MNS_PROVIDER_GRANTS` is retired and ignored. No legacy permission is silently copied to an unrestricted group.
The permission catalog keeps an empty `autoGrantProviders` field for wire compatibility. There is no composed automatic permission policy.
Apply the new migration and runtime grants before starting the updated API. Startup checks reject a missing provider-group table. An older application may restore its previous link policy, so rollback requires an explicit authorization review.

title: ADR Instructions
heading: ADR Instructions
text:
ADR Instructions
Consult the [decision index](README.md) and [authoring policy](authoring.md) before creating or changing an ADR.
Start new proposals with the [template](template.md) and `proposed` status. Acceptance is distinct from implementation completion.
Preserve accepted rationale, decisions, dates, and stable identifiers. Architectural changes require a new decision and explicit supersession, not rewritten history.
Retain meaningful alternatives, negative consequences, constraints, and evidence. Do not invent evaluations to fill the template.
Update current policy and reciprocal supersession references when an accepted architectural change requires them.

title: Authoring Architecture Decision Records
heading: Authoring Architecture Decision Records
text:
Authoring Architecture Decision Records
Use the [decision index](README.md) to search existing decisions and the [template](template.md) to draft a record. ADRs preserve decision history and rationale; current policy describes current architecture. Git, migrations, changelogs, design documents, and runbooks retain their separate responsibilities.

title: Authoring Architecture Decision Records
heading: When a decision needs an ADR
text:
When a decision needs an ADR
Create an ADR for a significant choice whose rationale a future contributor cannot reliably infer from implementation. Relevant effects include system boundaries, dependency direction, ownership, runtime/deployment topology, security, persistence, public contracts, cross-cutting technology, operational behavior, and long-term maintainability.
Consider the breadth, reversibility, long-term dependency, plausible alternatives, integrity/security implications, and risk of losing the reasoning. Ordinary local refactors, fixes, tests, small helpers, individual indexes, and routine dependency additions do not each need an ADR. Major technology choices generally do. Existing foundation policies do not each need retroactive ADRs.
An ADR records a sufficiently concrete architectural conclusion, not every discussion or rejected idea. It must not become a task tracker, changelog, runbook, detailed implementation design, or snapshot of volatile vendor data. A separate RFC system is not required. Bundle decisions only when their rationale and lifecycle belong together; avoid giant records deciding unrelated parts of the stack.

title: Authoring Architecture Decision Records
heading: Lifecycle and historical integrity
text:
Lifecycle and historical integrity
Status
Meaning
`proposed`
Under active consideration; implementation must not assume finality unless explicitly exploratory
`accepted`
Approved architectural direction; implementation and current documentation should align, allowing an explicit migration period
`rejected`
Considered and deliberately not adopted
`superseded`
Previously accepted, then replaced by another decision; link the replacement
`deprecated`
Historically relevant but no longer appropriate for new architecture; use sparingly when replacement is transitional or incomplete
Do not add statuses without a clear need. Normal transitions are proposed to accepted/rejected and accepted to superseded/deprecated. Do not normally revert historical decisions to proposed; create a new record when reconsidering them.
Accepted does not mean implemented or released. Track pending/partial/completed implementation through normal issues, tasks, or pull requests, not extra ADR statuses. Exploratory work and proofs of concept provide evidence but do not themselves establish acceptance. Long-lived production implementation should generally not rely on an unresolved major proposal.
Accepted substantive history should remain immutable. Non-semantic spelling, formatting, broken-link, and obvious-typo corrections may be acceptable, but must not change historical meaning. When architecture changes, create a new ADR. Retain the old record, mark it superseded, and add reciprocal `Supersedes` / `Superseded by` references. Keep the original date. For partial supersession, identify precisely what remains valid, what changed, and which decision replaces it.
Rejected records can preserve useful evaluation and constraints; a changed context can justify reconsideration in a new ADR. Do not treat rejection as a permanent prohibition. Purely local abandoned proposals may be removed before meaningful shared history; preserve broadly reviewed or referenced proposals as rejected where useful. Do not record every immediately dismissed idea.

title: Authoring Architecture Decision Records
heading: Identity and metadata
text:
Identity and metadata
Use monotonic numeric identifiers and descriptive English filenames of the form `NNNN-short-decision-title.md`. Numbers identify records, not importance, domain, priority, or version. Gaps are acceptable. Never reuse or renumber identifiers already in shared history. Resolve parallel numbering conflicts before merge; an unshared identifier may be changed.
Record title, status, date, context, decision, and consequences. For accepted records, the date should generally be the acceptance date. Titles should describe the decision rather than merely name a topic. Preserve identifiers once merged and referenced.
Simple Markdown metadata is the current format. `pnpm docs:check` validates filenames, matching titles/IDs, status, ISO dates, required sections, and index membership. Preserve these field names as tooling contracts. Supersession semantics still require review; no automatic numbering or supersession checker is implemented. ADR files remain canonical; avoid duplicate status stores or custom ADR software without a concrete need.

title: Authoring Architecture Decision Records
heading: Content and evidence
text:
Content and evidence
**Context:** explain the actual problem, relevant constraints, scope, timing, and assumptions. Avoid unnecessary implementation detail.
**Decision:** state the chosen direction clearly enough to understand independently of the alternatives.
**Rationale:** explain the material tradeoffs, evidence, and constraints. Distinguish confirmed evidence, reasoned tradeoffs, and assumptions.
**Alternatives:** describe serious alternatives considered; do not fabricate alternatives or evaluation evidence to fill a template.
**Consequences:** include benefits, costs, limitations, new responsibilities, security/operational effects, and reversibility or migration costs where relevant. Formal scoring is not required.
**References:** link relevant repository policy, earlier decisions, designs, benchmarks, proofs of concept, and durable evidence. Avoid unnecessary dependency graphs and large volatile datasets. Preserve enough explanation that disappearing external links do not destroy the rationale.
Use current evidence at decision time when product capability, support lifecycle, pricing, security status, or provider limits matter. Vendor documentation can support constraints but must not be the sole location of the explanation. Detailed implementation and operational migration steps normally belong outside the ADR.

title: Authoring Architecture Decision Records
heading: Creation, review, and acceptance
text:
Creation, review, and acceptance
Search the index and related policies for the same question, accepted direction, superseded decision, or rejected alternative. Determine whether this is an architectural decision rather than an implementation detail.
Allocate the next available identifier, copy the template, and use `proposed` status.
Document context, explicit direction, meaningful alternatives, rationale, constraints, and positive and negative consequences while the context is still known.
Review in proportion to impact: is the problem real, the complexity justified, and the choice consistent with existing architecture? Identify conflicts and intentional deviations explicitly.
Accept or reject through repository review. For a small team, review, merge, and accepted status are sufficient; do not add governance ceremony without a concrete need.
On acceptance, update affected current documentation and implement the selected direction with relevant verification. Do not retain rejected experimental paths unnecessarily.
For supersession, additionally identify changed constraints, reciprocal references, affected current policy, and compatibility/migration work. For rejection, record decisive reasons, preferred alternatives where applicable, and conditions that could justify reconsideration.
Retrospective ADRs should say the decision was already in effect. Record only known reasoning and state uncertainty rather than inventing a historical evaluation. Significant principle deviations belong in the decision and corresponding current-policy update. When later accepted decisions supersede older records, follow the replacement and current policy rather than treating the superseded record as current architecture.

title: Authoring Architecture Decision Records
heading: Maintenance and deferred mechanisms
text:
Maintenance and deferred mechanisms
Routine maintenance should be limited to permitted corrections and supersession metadata. Current architecture must remain discoverable without reading the entire chronological ADR history. Keep descriptive titles, explicit technologies/concepts, and useful related references.
Frontmatter, automatic numbering, generated indexing, status/supersession validation, approval workflows, and required reviewers remain tooling or organizational decisions. Introduce them only when justified. ADRs should preserve meaningful reasoning without becoming bureaucratic records for every change.

Use this index to locate governing decisions without reading the full history. Each linked record owns its status, decision, rationale, and consequences. Acceptance does not imply implementation; see [validation availability](../validation.md) and the [technology map](../architecture/technology-decisions.md).
For a new decision, read [authoring policy](authoring.md), inspect related records, and use the [proposed template](template.md). Current behavior belongs in the [policy index](../README.md), not in rewritten historical ADRs.

title: API Error Contract
heading: API Error Contract
text:
API Error Contract
[Task index](../README.md) · [API principles](principles.md) · [Error handling](../architecture/error-handling.md) · [Compatibility](versioning.md)
This policy owns public failure semantics. The API's [shared error registry, envelope schema, and responder](../../apps/api/src/errors.ts) and each composed module's registered codes are canonical; the [public registry composition](../../apps/api/src/error-registry.ts) gives each code exactly one owner and rejects any duplicate, even an identical definition, and the [generated error reference](../generated/api/errors.md) lists implemented codes, messages, categories, HTTP statuses, and retry classifications. Module route contracts declare expected operation errors. Follow [ADR-0007](../adr/0007-establish-api-contract-openapi-sdk-and-configuration-schema-strategy.md) when generating OpenAPI and SDK representations.

title: API Error Contract
heading: Error Envelope

title: API Error Contract
heading: Error Code Format
text:
Error Code Format
Public codes use stable semantic `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` names. Clients branch on codes and deliberately defined structured fields, never on message text or internal exception classes. Messages are safe human explanations and may change for clarity or product localization without changing the code's meaning. Canonical repository descriptions remain English.
Infrastructure identifiers such as SQLSTATE, ORM codes, provider exceptions, filesystem paths, or runtime class names are not public semantics. Map failures to the condition consumers need to understand. Reuse an existing code for the same meaning; do not create a code for every code path, collapse materially different consumer actions into one generic code, or reuse a retired code for a new meaning.

title: API Error Contract
heading: Error Code Ownership
text:
Error Code Ownership
The feature/application owner defines business failures; the API boundary owns cross-cutting public mappings. The registry provides one canonical definition, and operation metadata refers to it. The registry enumerates stable public conditions, not every possible database/network/library exception. Do not maintain an independent manual registry in prose or generated clients.
For a new code, determine its semantic owner, expected/unexpected category, public disclosure safety, consumer action, status mapping, retry implications, optional details, and compatibility impact. Update canonical code, operation declarations, tests, and generated references together. Each module's implementation conventions explain its authorization-sensitive classification order.

title: API Error Contract
heading: Validation Errors
text:
Validation Errors
The implemented validation response is `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` with the common envelope. Do not expose validator exceptions or echo submitted values. Structural validation is distinct from a valid request that conflicts with current domain state.
If field-level details become useful, add an explicit bounded schema to the canonical contract. Identify fields using a stable public request-path convention, never internal database/ORM paths; use stable reason codes where clients need to act and safe human text for explanation. Define multiple-failure bounds and unknown-field behavior. Returning every issue in an attacker-controlled payload must not create an unbounded response.

title: API Error Contract
heading: Mapping and disclosure
text:
Mapping and disclosure
HTTP status conveys broad protocol meaning; public codes convey application semantics. The [generated registry](../generated/api/errors.md) is the current status mapping. Validation uses `400`, authentication `401`, permission denial `403`, absent/hidden resources `404`, state/version conflicts `409`, rate limiting `429`, unexpected failures `500`, and service unavailability `503` where declared.
Authentication and authorization failures follow their [security policies](../security/authentication.md). Avoid account enumeration and disclosure of hidden resource existence, cross-tenant data, claims, or policy internals. An absent and inaccessible resource may deliberately share `404`; test that behavior.
Expected domain conflicts, stale versions, and incompatible idempotency-key reuse are explicit outcomes. Distinguish safe replay from a conflicting new intent. They should not become internal incidents simply because code represents them as exceptions.
Translate known database constraints at the persistence/application boundary according to business meaning. Unexpected database failures stay unexpected; do not disguise every exception as invalid user input.
Translate provider business rejection separately from dependency unavailability, configuration failure, or unknown outcome. Expose vendor-specific distinctions only when consumers need them, never raw provider content.
Use a safe generic error for unexpected failures. Never serialize arbitrary exceptions, stack traces, SQL, secret values, internal paths/hostnames, or diagnostic dumps. Do not return ordinary API failures as hidden error objects inside `200` responses.
Public status is not internal severity: expected denials may matter to security monitoring, and a transient dependency failure may be operationally serious. [Error reporting](../reliability/error-reporting.md) owns that distinction.

title: API Error Contract
heading: Unknown Outcome
text:
Unknown Outcome
A timeout, disconnect, or commit error may leave the caller uncertain whether a write or external effect occurred. Retryability cannot be inferred from HTTP status or transient infrastructure failure alone. Define whether the operation is known not to have occurred, safely replayable, or requires state reconciliation. Introduce a distinct public unknown-outcome code only when consumers need different handling.
A public retry hint, if introduced, must be machine-readable, bounded, and accurate for the operation. Rate-limit guidance must not disclose anti-abuse internals. Never imply a non-idempotent write is safe to repeat merely because the registry classifies a failure as transient. Each module's recovery conventions own its create replay and mutation reconciliation behavior.

title: API Error Contract
heading: Details and additional delivery modes
text:
Details and additional delivery modes
Every public details object needs a typed schema and a consumer purpose. Include only information safe for that caller; omit record dumps, protected resource/tenant identifiers, authorization evaluation, credentials, and provider payloads. Cross-cutting correlation/retry metadata should remain distinguishable from domain details. Once consumed, field meaning and shape are compatibility-sensitive.
When additional modes are introduced:
Mode
Error requirement
Webhook or upload
Follow the operation/provider contract while minimizing signature-validation or scanning details. Bound and classify upload failures explicitly.
Asynchronous work
A successful acceptance response does not guarantee eventual success. Externally visible job status maps worker failures to stable public semantics, never worker exceptions.
Batch/partial success
Define atomic versus partial processing and item identity in an operation-specific result. Do not ambiguously overload the ordinary single-error envelope.

title: API Error Contract
heading: Diagnostics and consumer behavior
text:
Diagnostics and consumer behavior
Report an unexpected occurrence once at its authoritative boundary. Preserve useful internal causal evidence only within [redaction rules](../security/telemetry-redaction.md); preservation never authorizes raw exception-message or stack export. The current runtime records allowlisted diagnostic fields rather than arbitrary error content. Expected validation, business, and access failures may contribute to safe metrics/security/audit signals without becoming unexpected incidents.
Clients and SDKs must preserve structured error semantics and correlation, and provide a safe fallback for unknown codes. Application consumers should not depend on framework-specific transport exceptions for business meaning. Product code decides whether to display safe server copy or localized client text; it must not parse that copy. The current thin SDK exposes generated response/error typing without adding a separate error-class hierarchy.
Code meaning, status mappings, details, categories where consumed, and retry behavior require [compatibility review](versioning.md). Adding a code can break exhaustive consumers; renaming/removing a code or changing meaning is potentially breaking. Optional details are only additive if actual clients tolerate them.

title: API Error Contract
heading: Change and verification checklist
text:
Change and verification checklist
Inspect the registry, similar conditions, owning operation, actual consumers, authorization/disclosure policy, and compatibility commitments.
Define the safe semantic mapping and outcome/retry behavior. Add details only when needed, with explicit schema and size limits.
Verify the real transport envelope, status, code, safe message, correlation, hidden-resource handling, and relevant failure paths. Test absent/invalid/expired credentials and other lifecycle states only where that mechanism exists.
Inject unexpected failures and assert that secrets, SQL, provider data, input values, stacks, and internal paths do not escape. Verify one appropriate diagnostic event and safe retry metadata if present.
Regenerate and check the registry/OpenAPI/SDK references through [validation](../validation.md). Preserve current checks for registered unique codes, operation declarations, and freshness; extend checks for any new detail schemas or released compatibility obligations.
